data.final_week_advice: In the final week, focus on timed practice and targeted review of any lingering uncertainties to maximize exam readiness.
data.summary: This 5‑week plan tackles the student’s weak Unit 3 first, then cycles through the remaining units, ending with a mixed review week. Each week uses 15 hours of focused study, including concrete tasks and the single available live class in week 2.

weeks.focus: Start with Unit 3 concepts and build momentum.
tasks: Read textbook sections on translational kinetic energy and work; solve 5 worked examples for each topic.
Do 10 practice problems on work and kinetic energy, then self‑grade using the scoring rubric.
Create a concept map linking kinetic energy, work, and potential energy.

weeks.focus: Apply Unit 3 knowledge and attend live class.
tasks: Watch the live class on conservation of energy and power; take detailed notes.
After class, solve 8 practice problems on conservation of energy scenarios.
Review class notes and identify any gaps; write 3 questions to discuss with the teacher.
Read sections on impulse and conservation of momentum; summarize key formulas.
Do 10 free‑response problems on elastic and inelastic collisions; grade with rubric.
Create flashcards for impulse-momentum theorem and collision types.

weeks.focus: Introduce rotational dynamics and energy of rotating systems.
tasks: Solve 5 problems on rotational kinematics and connecting linear/rotational motion.
Work through 5 rotational kinetic energy problems; compare with linear energy results.
Write a short explanation of how torque relates to angular acceleration.
Take a 60‑minute timed practice test covering all units; record score.
Review incorrect answers and revisit relevant textbook sections.
Create a summary sheet of all key formulas and concepts for quick reference.
